summary: Klamath County, OR steel tower bought as 80 ft in 1935 and extended to 120 ft; the register dates it 1933; gone by 1969, with footings recorded on a 2022 visit.

facts.design: Aermotor steel tower, bought as 80 ft and extended to 120 ft; 12x16 living quarters cabin
facts.status_note: Tower and cabin gone by 1969 per the register; footings and the lookout site were seen on a 2022 visit
facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service per the register; Klamath Indian Agency / Winema National Forest per Forest Lookouts

visit.trail_note: The 2022 visit lists access as drive-up or close; a spur road leads to the top. The sources read do not say who controls the land now.

events.note: Register and firelookout.com date the tower and cabin to 1933; the Forest Service reports quoted by Forest Lookouts describe the work in 1935-1937
80-foot Aermotor steel tower bought from the Aermotor Company of Chicago; a survey then called for 120 feet and a 40-foot extension
12x16 living quarters cabin completed in November
Tower complete except guy wires and lightning protection wires
Two fires caused by careless smokers on the Klamath Reservation on Sunday, July 28; one about a mile northwest of the lookout was controlled by grazing permit holders and Indian Service officers
Advertisement for bids by the Klamath Tribes naming the 120-foot steel tower and 12x16 cabin
Lookout buildings sold to a Lakeview buyer for $35; contract required removal by December 30, 1969
Gone by 1969 per the register; firelookout.com says 'Gone 1969'
Registered June 4, 2011 on the Former Fire Lookout Sites register
Visited 2022 per WillhiteWeb: footings at the lookout site, an outhouse and a phone insulator on the final spur road

corrections.why: 24.4 m is the original 80-foot tower. The register gives a 120-foot steel tower, and the Forest Service reports quoted by Forest Lookouts say a 40-foot extension was needed, so 120 ft (36.6 m) is the height of the finished tower.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and firelookout.com date the tower and cabin to 1933. The Forest Lookouts page quotes 1935-1937 Forest Service and Indian Service reports (purchase in 1935, cabin in November 1936, tower complete by 1937). The story reports both and does not pick one; the 1933 event is kept with a note.

The register lists the U.S. Forest Service. Forest Lookouts lists the Klamath Indian Agency and Winema National Forest, and WillhiteWeb describes an Indian Forest Service station with the 1959 bids made by the Klamath Tribes. Both are recorded in facts.agency.

notes_for_editor: The brief's height (24.4 m) is the original 80-ft tower; corrected to 120 ft. The construction date is disputed: 1933 in the register and firelookout.com, 1935-1937 in the Forest Service reports quoted by Forest Lookouts. Access level is left out: a 2022 visit lists drive-up access, but no source read says who controls the land now. A Herald and News column (heraldandnews.com, 'What's the point at Modoc Point?') reportedly says its writers found no evidence of an old lookout; the fetch returned HTTP 429, so it is not cited. The brief's agency and access fields are not corrected; the agency conflict is recorded above. No new photos found.
